description:
## Problem

Catseye propagates taint through cryptographic hash functions (SHA256, HMAC, etc.), treating the hash output as still tainted. This causes mass false positives when hashes are used for safe filenames, cache keys, and identifiers.

## Evidence

From quickheadlines scan (2026-06-01), 134 findings in favicon_storage.cr alone:
- URL -> SHA256 hash -> filename -> filepath flagged as PathTraversal
- URL -> hash -> cache key operations flagged as CommandInjection
- 24 findings in color_extractor.cr for cache operations on hash-derived keys
- 11 findings in storage/cache_utils.cr
- 12 findings in storage/feed_cache.cr

## Example

```crystal
hash = favicon_hash_for_url(url)      # URL taint -> hash still tainted
filename = favicon_filename(hash, ext) # tainted -> safe name like abc123.png
filepath = File.join(favicon_dir, filename) # flagged as PathTraversal
```

## Expected Behavior

SHA256 and other cryptographic hash functions should be recognized as sanitizers that break taint chains. The output of a one-way hash is not controllable by the input beyond collision resistance.

## Affected Rules
- PathTraversal (126 findings)
- CommandInjection (123 findings)
- ScentLeakage (partial)

## Suggested Fix

Add crypto hash functions (OpenSSL::Digest, SHA256, SHA1, MD5, Digest.new, etc.) to the sanitizer/sink recognition list so taint stops at hash boundaries.
title: Taint sanitization: recognize cryptographic hash functions as taint sinks
